input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives us a convenience right on one month's notice effective at the end of a calendar month (better than the 60–90 day fallback), and IBM has no mid-term convenience exit: its only termination rights are for material breach (3.3) and non-renewal at the end of a term on 90 days' notice (3.2). The single material gap is Section 3.4(b), which conditions our convenience termination on uncapped early termination charges set out in Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, so the fallback three-months cap on any early-termination fee is not met. We therefore sit at the fallback on every other element and have made the shortest change to add the cap; we did not press the preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is noted but not the basis of this flag.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three (3) months' charges.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that convenience termination should carry no penalty; as a fallback we can accept an early termination charge capped at three months' charges, so we have added that cap to Section 3.4(b) while leaving the rest of the clause unchanged.
proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges at three months' charges
